title: Automated warm-standby health probes and prioritized region routing
creator: Aisha Mehta
description:
Goal: Implement automated warm-standby readiness probes and a prioritized region routing policy to enable deterministic multi-region failover for customers using tiered routing (hosted/dedicated/private). This ticket covers: 1) a health-check orchestration layer that can run synthetic probes against warm-standby pools, 2) a readiness scoring model for standby nodes (capacity, model-variant compatibility, KV cache priming state), and 3) integration with the smart routing policy engine so that routing decisions prefer healthy primary region targets and only failover to warm-standby regions that meet readiness thresholds.

Background: During the Feb outage on us-west-2 we observed slow manual failovers and a number of customer requests hitting cold model variants in warm regions causing latency spikes. We need deterministic automation to reduce RTO and avoid regressions to incompatible model variants.

Scope: - Probe definitions (latency p95, inference success, model-variant match check, KV-resume sync) - Readiness scoring (0-100) and threshold gating - Orchestration state machine for probe cadence and escalating remedial actions (cache-priming, instance warming, autoscale triggers) - API flags for Console and routing policy rules to consume readiness state - Observability: dashboards, alerts, and audit logs for failover decisions

Non-goals: full cross-region state replication or making warm-standby the permanent serving path (this ticket does not change the default primary-first routing policy).
acceptance_criteria: Automated probes run against warm-standby pools at a configurable cadence and emit metrics to CloudMetrics (latency p50/p95, error rate, model-mismatch count)
Readiness score computed and stored for each warm-standby pool (score exposed via API and used by routing engine)
Routing engine respects readiness threshold: only failover to warm region pools above configured score and with compatible model variants
Console shows health summary and last-probe timestamps; alert fires if readiness falls below emergency threshold for >2 minutes

Playbook verified in runbook rehearsal: a simulated primary-region outage should cause automated failover to ready warm-standby in <45s for standard tier customers and <20s for dedicated tier where reserved capacity exists

notes: Design trade-offs: polling cadence vs cost — default cadence set to 30s with exponential backoff when stability is high to control metric ingestion costs.
Priming strategy: when readiness < threshold an automated cache-priming job can be queued; priming is best-effort and has a cost budget per account (configurable).

Compatibility mapping: model-family + quantization-level + tokenizer-hash used to determine 'compatible model variant'. If no exact match, routing can optionally allow 'graceful-degrade' variants with lower quality but must be explicit per-customer policy.
Operational runbook steps included in linked PDF; rehearsals required once per quarter for critical customers.
